perspective:
Henry’s available information:

- Henry is a Business Analyst at the hotel. Charles Beyene is his colleague, a hotel security guard; they work together on operational/security matters with mutual professional respect.
- While personally reviewing security footage, Henry saw a group in the hotel lobby behaving suspiciously. He felt growing anxiety about a possible threat to guests and the hotel’s reputation.
- Henry told Charles about the suspicious group. Charles said they should review the footage together and approach the situation discreetly.
- After reviewing the footage with Charles, Henry saw what he believed was the group passing around suspicious objects. He urged action. Charles appeared unconvinced/suggested it might be a misunderstanding, then agreed to keep a closer eye on them and act if things escalated.
- Through further analysis of the security footage and additional information from hotel staff, Henry learned the suspicious activity was actually a group of guests participating in a scavenger hunt organized by a local event company. He apologized to Charles for the earlier tension; Charles said no worries and encouraged open communication.
- Henry received a tip from another hotel staff member about possible internal thefts. He suspected the real issue might involve hotel staff and decided to investigate discreetly to avoid false accusations.
- Henry discussed with Charles a plan to discreetly review internal security logs and employee records. Charles agreed they should gather information quietly.
- Henry’s investigation led him to identify a staff member manipulating inventory records. He decided to confront that staff member with the evidence in a controlled environment.
- Henry told the staff member that, although they might be facing personal issues, the matter was serious and needed proper handling. The staff member said they were willing to cooperate fully and did not want to cause more trouble for the hotel.
